newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Ford F.N. targets Venezuelan small car market.
newsitem.headline: Ford F.N. targets Venezuelan small car market.

text.p: Ford Motor Co's Venezuelan affiliate aims to raise its share of the Venezuelan car market from 20 percent to 25 percent with the launch of the compact Fiesta model.
"Our aim in the short term is that one out of four cars sold in Venezuela is a Ford," Ford de Venezuela President Jose Manuel Machado said on Monday.
He spoke at the official launch of the Fiesta, at Ford's only plant in Venezuela, in the central industrial city of Valencia.
"We hope to build 10,000 Fiesta this year," he told a news conference, to bring Ford's annual production to 30,000 units.

Ford last year produced just above 20,000 cars, giving it the leading position in Venezuela but the second in terms of market share behind General Motors Corp. About a third of Ford's cars were exported to Andean pact nations Colombia and Ecuador.
Machado said Ford expected Venezuela's depressed car market, with 61,602 vehicles sold last year from 80,391 in 1995, to pick up sharply as the country emerges from economic recession.
"Total sales this year could be near 100,000," he predicted, and about 300,000 including Colombia and Ecuador.

In a measure of confidence in the local car market, Ford plans to introduce three other new models this year in Venezuela. The company will invest $30 million at its 35-year-old Valencia plant to assemble the Fiesta.
In Colombia, Ford held 5.8 percent of total sales last year, up from 3.6 percent in 1995, "and we want to take it to 10 percent in the short term," Machado said.
The Fiesta, one of the best selling cars in Europe in the small car segment over the past four years, will be available to retail customers in Venezuela and Colombia from March 1.

It was introduced in neighboring Brazil in mid-1996 where the company is planning to start assembling its sub-compact Ka model from April. The Ka, a so-called minicar derived from the Fiesta, will probably hit Venezuelan and Colombian markets before the year 2000, Ford officials said, but no date has been set.
